successor: Provisional Government of Hawaii / Republic of Hawaii (annexed by USA 1898)
source2: US National Archives, educator lesson on the Hawaiian anti-annexation petition (overthrow, Republic, Newlands Resolution) - https://www.archives.gov/education/lessons/hawaii-petition
notes: Jan 1893 resident Committee of Safety overthrew queen in coup backed by US Marines; Provisional Government, Republic 1894. Database end 1898 is US annexation by joint resolution. T2 arguable if US role counted. Q4: 1887 Bayonet Constitution.

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Guti' (also 'Mesopotamia: end of the Akkad dynasty') - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Guti
source2: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, 'Art of the Akkadian Period' - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/akka/hd_akka.htm
notes: Succession quarrels after Shar-kali-sharri, cities broke away, last kings held only Agade area; Britannica says Guti overthrew empire (priority rule T2). Gutian role debated. Database dates ~64 yrs lower than middle chronology (end c.2154 BCE).

source2: Ernst Badian, 'Darius v. Darius III', Encyclopaedia Iranica VII/1, 1994 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/darius-v
notes: Alexander won Gaugamela 331, took Babylon and Susa, destroyed Persepolis; Darius III killed by Bessus 330, ending dynasty. Q4: Bagoas murdered Arses and sons (336); revolts in Egypt and Babylon.

source2: Roy Rosenzweig Center for History and New Media (GMU) and American Social History Project (CUNY), Liberty, Equality, Fraternity: 'Monarchy Falls' - https://revolution.chnm.org/exhibits/show/liberty--equality--fraternity/monarchy-falls
notes: Parisian insurrection of 10 Aug 1792 deposed Louis XVI; Convention abolished monarchy 21 Sep 1792, republic proclaimed. Database end 1815 is wrong (perhaps conflating Restoration). Q4: fiscal crisis and revolution from 1787-89.

successor: Ayutthaya (Siamese suzerainty over a restored Cambodian monarchy)
source1: Nhim Sotheavin, 'Considerations Regarding the Fall of Longvek', UDAYA Journal of Khmer Studies 15, 2020 - https://www.yosothor.org/uploads/images/Udaya/Udaya_pdf/Udaya-Yosothor/No-15-2020/ARTICLES/02-02_Nhim_Sotheavin_Udaya15_2021.pdf
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Cambodia: Tai and Vietnamese hegemony' - https://www.britannica.com/place/Cambodia/Tai-and-Vietnamese-hegemony
notes: Ayutthaya army sacked Lovek late 1593/Jan 1594; king Satha fled to Laos, viceroy taken hostage; later kings ruled under Siamese protection. Royal line continued, so T0 arguable. Q4: factional dispute over Satha's succession plans.

source1: Naomi Standen, 'The Five Dynasties', Cambridge History of China vol. 5 pt 1, Cambridge UP 2009 - https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/cambridge-history-of-china/five-dynasties/BED8234EA917268392A83E07FFE08EE7
notes: Power divided among regional governors and warlords after Huang Chao rebellion; Tang control of central Yellow River valley extinguished by 907 when governor Zhu Wen forced abdication. Internal throughout; T1c (usurpation) is an alternative reading.

source2: US Library of Congress, Russia: A Country Study, 'Early Imperial Russia' - http://countrystudies.us/russia/4.htm
notes: Database period split only; Romanov rule and imperial apparatus continued unbroken 1613-1917. 1775 marks Catherine II's provincial reform. Q4: Pugachev rebellion 1773-75 (Britannica 'Pugachov').

successor: Ghurid Sultanate (Mu'izz al-Din Muhammad; Delhi Sultanate from 1206)
source2: C. E. Bosworth, 'Ghurids', Encyclopaedia Iranica X/6, 2001 - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/ghurids
notes: Jayachandra defeated and killed by Muhammad of Ghur at Chandawar (1194; database 1193); Kannauj plundered 1194; remnant under Harishchandra to c.1197. Iranica confirms Ghurid conquests down Ganges valley. No internal crisis documented.

successor: Rival Khmer principalities (Land and Water Chenla); reunified as Early Angkor by Jayavarman II, 802
notes: Many small kingdoms 7th-9th c.; Chinese sources record Land/Water Chenla split (after c.707); Jayavarman II reunified 802. Database 825 too late. Claimed Javanese suzerainty c.800 is disputed. Chronology uncertain.

Database period split only; core is Venice (capital), not Crete. Doge-led republican government continued unbroken until last doge deposed 1797 after French conquest. No major internal crisis 1513-1563 found.
